items.title: Howard Mandel interviewed by Monk Rowe, Toronto, Canada, January 9, 2003
items.q: I was exposed to some early Truffaut and Goddard, that sort of thing.

ctx.x: Well I was listening to Ramsey Lewis and “The In Crowd” and rhythm & blues music, it was on the local radio. I grew up in Chicago and I lived in a community that was on the South Side of Chicago so it was a neighborhood that was divided by Stony Island Avenue which is a large commercial street, and on one side was the black neighborhood and on the other side was the white neighborhood, but we went to the same grammar schools. And I just didn’t understand what the distinction was, why there was this kind of divide…

me akin to the movies I was watching, I was exposed to some early Truffaut and Goddard, that sort of thing. And I saw those kinds of connections. So I didn’t really see it as like swing or bebop, I just knew it as dramatic, fractured, abstracted, fast, that sort of thing.
I understand you took some piano.
